fields.statement: At b63f7c18 I built rhiza to a scratch path and ran it by hand on this repo's .rhiza. log 01M5TYGK7EFHKPB9JG3A2MH2G2 (three change sets) --limit 2 printed two change sets and 'next: rhiza log 01M5TYGK7EFHKPB9JG3A2MH2G2 --limit 2 --cursor <c>'; that cursor's page held the third with no next_cursor and the same target and view; the two pages concatenated equal --all. --limit 0 gave the default page; --limit -1, --limit 1001, --cursor zz and --cursor !!! exited 2 with 'next: rhiza describe log'. log --json and api call log printed the same bytes. go test of log-paged and describe-golden scripts: ok.

At b63f7c18 with a scratch build on this repo (4 groups, 18 change sets): paging roadmap with --limit 1, 4, 5 and 7 to the end gave exactly the (group kind, intent, change set) entries of --all, in order, each once. --limit 3 split milestone-25 and page 2 repeated its '## milestone-25' heading before Backlog. --limit 0 equals the default; --limit -1, --limit 1001 and --cursor zz exited 2 ('bad cursor "zz": give a next_cursor from roadmap'). roadmap --json and api call roadmap printed the same bytes. TestRoadmapOverAPageIsReadWhole (health), TestReadsARoadmapOverAPageWhole (roadmap app), TestRoadmapTabReadsARoadmapOverAPageWhole (model app) and roadmap-paged.txtar pass.

At b63f7c18 with a scratch build on this repo, why 01M5SWRSPVMK689DD23KH7KP0Z (43 decisions, 5 sources, 1 change set) paged with --limit 1, 7, 42, 44 and 48 (splitting at and across list boundaries): every page carried the --all node and view, the concatenated decisions, sources and change sets equal --all in order, and the last page had no next_cursor. --limit 0 equals the default; --all ignores --limit; --limit -1, --limit 1001 and --cursor zz exited 2. why --json and api call why printed the same bytes. why-paged.txtar passes.
